brief.headline: Memory Supercycle Intact: DRAM +13–18% Q3, HBM3E Tight Into 2027, CoWoS Gap Narrowing to 10%
brief.summary: <cite index="8-1">DRAM contract prices projected to rise 13–18% QoQ in Q3 2026, with NAND Flash up 10–15%</cite>, extending the AI-driven rally despite consumer demand softening. <cite index="5-3,5-4">SK Hynix began HBM4 mass-production supply in Q2 2026 and reports yield already near mature HBM3E levels</cite>, while <cite index="1-2">both SK Hynix and Samsung are prioritizing HBM4 ramps, keeping HBM3E supply tight and lagging demand</cite>. <cite index="18-4">Hyperscaler quarterly capex hit $112B in Q1 2026</cite>, with <cite index="25-4">Microsoft disclosing ~$80B unfulfilled Azure backlog due to power constraints</cite>. <cite index="26-10">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap expected to narrow from ~20% currently to ~10% by end-2026</cite>, though <cite index="35-4">CoWoS demand still exceeds supply by 40–50%</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral to slight SK Hynix outperform. <cite index="5-3,5-4,5-5">SK Hynix confirmed HBM4 mass-production yield near HBM3E levels and is stably increasing capacity</cite>, while <cite index="2-2,2-3">Samsung finished HBM4 development and cleared Production Readiness Approval (PRA)</cite> but hasn't confirmed volume shipments. <cite index="7-1">Goldman assessed SK Hynix will maintain dominant HBM3/HBM3E position with over 50% total HBM market share through at least 2026</cite>. Both names sold off <cite index="41-1,41-5,41-6">~8% today (Aug 3) after a record 17.91% rally on July 31</cite>, with <cite index="41-9,41-10">brokerages cutting target prices: Shinhan lowered Samsung to 450k from 590k, SK Hynix to 2.7m from 4.2m; Samsung Securities cut Samsung to 400k from 500k, SK Hynix to 3m from 3.5m</cite>. Relative edge to SK Hynix on HBM execution visibility, but both trade at ~50% of consensus targets post-correction.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="8-1">Q3 2026 DRAM contract pricing +13–18% QoQ, NAND +10–15% QoQ</cite>, decelerating from <cite index="12-2,12-7">Q2's +58–63% DRAM and +70–75% NAND QoQ gains</cite>. <cite index="10-5,10-6">Samsung and SK Hynix, ~70% of global DRAM, signaled no aggressive capacity expansion, prioritizing profitability over volume</cite>. <cite index="8-9,8-10">AI inference and hyperscale data center demand keeps DRAM/NAND constrained as suppliers shift capacity to higher-margin server products, leaving less for consumer memory</cite>. <cite index="12-10">Cloud providers securing bulk supply through long-term agreements; meaningful capacity expansion not expected until late 2027</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-2">Samsung and SK Hynix prioritizing HBM4 ramps keeps HBM3E supply tight and lagging demand</cite>. <cite index="1-7">2026 HBM revenue mix forecast ~55% HBM4, 45% HBM3E, with HBM4 beginning in Q3 to rapidly absorb HBM3E demand</cite>. <cite index="5-3,5-4">SK Hynix began HBM4 mass-production supply in Q2 2026, with yield and quality near mature HBM3E levels</cite>; <cite index="5-6">HBM4E sample supply completed, targeting 2027 mass production</cite>. <cite index="2-2,2-3,2-5">Samsung finished HBM4 development, cleared Production Readiness Approval (PRA), and shipped samples to Nvidia for Rubin platform evaluation</cite>. <cite index="1-4,1-5">HBM3E prices holding despite HBM4 entry due to ongoing H200/ASIC launches; H200 China export approval drove unexpected HBM3E demand surge (six HBM3E stacks per H200)</cite>. <cite index="4-8">SK Hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples at 16Gbps per pin, 20%+ power efficiency improvement, 17% better heat resistance via Advanced MR-MUF</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix HBM4 yield nears HBM3E levels; unveils iHBM cooling tech cutting thermal resistance 30%
news_pulse.implication: Production readiness for HBM4 de-risks 2H26 revenue ramp; iHBM positions SK Hynix for HBM5 thermal challenges and competitive moat vs Samsung.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap to narrow from 20% to 10% by end-2026 as capacity expands 60%+
news_pulse.implication: Easing CoWoS bottleneck supports Nvidia Blackwell/Rubin ramp and incremental HBM attach; TSMC capacity reaching 115–140k wpm by end-2026.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler Q1 2026 capex hits $112B; Microsoft raises 2026 guidance by $25B citing component price inflation
news_pulse.implication: Memory ASP tailwind embedded in hyperscaler guidance; Azure $80B backlog confirms demand visibility but power constraints cap near-term fulfillment.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +13–18% Q3 2026, NAND +10–15% QoQ; rally decelerating from Q2's +58–63% DRAM surge
news_pulse.implication: Sequential pricing gains slowing but remain double-digit; server DRAM supply discipline and LTA lock-up sustaining premium through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix shares down ~8% Aug 3 after record +17.91% KOSPI rally July 31; brokers cut targets 20–30%
news_pulse.implication: Profit-taking after extreme volatility (July 31 SK Hynix +30%, Samsung +27% intraday); stocks now ~50% of consensus targets post-cuts, valuation reset likely.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung reportedly finished HBM4 development, cleared PRA; samples exceed Nvidia 11Gbps requirement
news_pulse.implication: Samsung closing HBM execution gap vs SK Hynix; faster HBM4 variant (+40% performance) possible mid-Feb 2026 announcement boosts Rubin attach odds.

news_pulse.headline: ADATA warns DRAM +20–30%, NAND +35–40% price hikes in Q3 2026; shortages expected through 2028
news_pulse.implication: Channel pricing supporting OEM contract gains; memory shortage duration extending beyond hyperscaler capex wave suggests structural under-capacity.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia secures ~60% of 2026 CoWoS capacity (595k wafers); 515k from TSMC, 80k from Amkor/ASE
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia Blackwell/Rubin ramp locked through 2026; remaining 40% split among Broadcom (15%), AMD, hyperscaler ASICs—tight allocation supports HBM premium pricing.

brief.derivatives_signal: Elevated realized vol persists. <cite index="41-1">KOSPI down 4.88% to 6,273 today after surging 17.91% on July 31</cite>; <cite index="38-1,38-2">SK Hynix +29.7% and Samsung +26.8% on July 31 marked best single-day gains on record</cite>. Implied vol likely elevated; use ratio spreads or calendar spreads to fade vol premium. Watch Korea circuit-breaker triggers if foreign institutional selling accelerates.
